title: Tenant initialization and observability orchestration for VPC private deployments
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This guide describes the recommended operator-driven sequence for tenant initialization (first-boot and ongoing warmstarts) and the observability orchestration that must be applied for Redwood private VPC deployments. It consolidates the operator bundle (preflight, staged model warmstart, KV cache priming, and telemetry gating) into an auditable runbook so field operators and customer operators follow the same safe pattern.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce SLA risk and mean time to healthy (MTTH) for newly commissioned tenants in VPC/private deployments by providing a reproducible initialization flow and a mandatory observability contract.
- Scope: Applies to all private VPC customer installs and self-hosted operator handoffs where Redwood provides the operator bundle (control plane or delegated operator). This does not replace specific customer firewall or change control requirements.

Audience:
Primary: deployment engineers, field operators, customer NOC engineers. Secondary: SREs and product engineers involved in private deploy rollouts.

Owner and escalation:
- Document owner: Engineering — Private Deployments team
- Primary contact for approvals: Asha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Escalation path: Operator on-call -> Private-deploy SRE -> Platform infra -> Product security if telemetry gating is blocked

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Healthy tenant ready to serve production traffic with validated latency SLOs and telemetry within 30 minutes of completion for small-capacity installs (up to 4 GPUs).
- Observability contract satisfied: metrics, traces, and logs are streaming to the tenant-specific ingest endpoint; synthetic probes show end-to-end success 3/3 times.

Prerequisites and preflight checks (operator checklist):
1) Customer connectivity confirmed (BGP/peer, cross-connect tested).
2) KMS/HSM credentials provisioned and validated (KMS handshake successful).
3) Image and artifact signature verification passed (SHA256 match and signature vendor attest).
4) Required quotas/capacity reserved: GPU counts, local disk, and network egress budget confirmed.
5) Telemetry endpoint and redact/PII policy agreed and configured.

Architecture overview (high level):
- The operator bundle performs the following orchestration phases: 1) preflight & attestation, 2) control-plane handshake, 3) tenant core service boot (API gateway, routing), 4) model artifact download & integrity check, 5) staged warmstart (KV cache priming → model weight verifications → model load), 6) telemetry gating and synthetic validation, 7) traffic ramp and handoff.

Operator sequence (detailed steps):
1. Preflight (automated): run ./operator preflight --tenant <TENANT_ID>. This produces a preflight report (preflight-<TENANT_ID>.json) with green/yellow/red indicators.
2. Attestation: verify hardware and image signatures. CLI example:
   curl -sS -X POST https://operator.local/api/v1/attest -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"image":"sha256:..."}'
3. Network handshake: validate cross-connect and DNS entries. Commands:
   - dig +short controlplane.<tenant>.redwood.internal
   - traceroute -m 15 <control-plane-ip>
4. Artifact staging: pull model tarball to cache node, verify signature, and compute model fingerprint. Example bash snippet:
   sha256sum model.tar.gz | tee model.sha256
   gpg --verify model.tar.gz.sig model.tar.gz
5. KV cache priming: run the priming job with a curated prompt set (see 'Priming dataset' below). This step uses controlled synthetic traffic to populate prefix caches and the attention KV store to reduce first-request tail latency.
6. Model warmload: load model into GPU memory in low-priority mode, validate init loss < threshold and run 3 inference sanity checks. If failures occur, operator can fallback to quantized-compatible variant.
7. Telemetry gating: enable full telemetry ingest only after synthetic probe passes. Until then, run in telemetry-buffered mode and hold the metrics export key in operator vault.
8. Traffic ramp: 0→10→50→100% traffic ramp over configurable windows (default 5 min per step). Use circuit-breakers for each step.
9. Handoff: mark tenant state = active and notify account team with the handoff template.

Priming dataset and priming job contract:
- The priming dataset is a curated set of 200 prompts reflecting the customer’s expected prompt patterns (token length distribution, function-calling patterns). The operator must: 1) ensure redaction for PII, 2) run at 0.1 qps to avoid capacity spikes, 3) tag the run as synthetic in telemetry (label synthetic=true).
- The priming job should accept these parameters: dataset_path (S3 URI), concurrency (1–8), qps_target, and max_tokens_per_prompt.

Observability contract (required signals):
- Metrics (every 10s): token_throughput, request_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_memory_utilization, model_load_time.
- Traces: distributed traces must include operator-init-span, model-load-span, priming-job-span, and request-endpoint spans with sampling rate 100% for the initialization window and 1% steady-state.
- Logs: operator and runtime logs must include structured JSON events with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, trace_id, level, component, message, and error_code if applicable.
- Synthetic probes: probe success ratio 100% for 3 sequential probes before telemetry gating.

Healthcheck response schema (example):
{"status":"ok","checks":{"model_loaded":"ok","kv_cache":"primed","telemetry_ingest":"buffering","latency_p95_ms":45}}

(Operators should assert model_loaded == ok and kv_cache in ["primed","partial"] before ramping traffic.)

Acceptance table (operator must validate):
| Item | Target | Pass condition |
|------|--------|----------------|
| Model load time | <= 90s | model_load_time <= 90s |
| kv cache hit rate | >= 70% | kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.7 |
| p95 latency | <= 150ms | request_latency_p95 <= 150 |
| Telemetry delivery | 3/3 probes | probe success == 3 |

Rollout and rollback procedures:
- Controlled rollout: Start with canary tenant routes (5% traffic), monitor SLOs for 10 minutes. If errors or p95 increases > 2x baseline, step rollback procedure.
- Fast rollback: operator trigger ./operator rollback --tenant <TENANT_ID> --to-stamp <ARTIFACT_STAMP>. Rollback reverses model load and re-activates previous kv cache snapshot.
- For stateful kv-cache mismatches: Evict newest cache and re-prime from snapshot. Avoid partial rollback without operator approval.

Observability gating failure modes and remediation:
- Telemetry backpressure: put runtime into telemetry-buffered mode (buffer duration 1h) and continue serving reads-only until ingestion restored. Notify compliance if PII-sensitive fields were buffered.
- Model artifact mismatch: quarantine reload and fall back to quantized-compatible model variant; open a ticket with "model-artifact-integrity" tag.
- KV priming failures: run the priming job with reduced concurrency (concurrency=1) and extended timeout (2x). If still failing, collect pprof and heap profiles and escalate to runtime team.

Automation snippets (Kubernetes job example):
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: tenant-priming-{{TENANT_ID}}
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: priming
        image: registry.redwood/ops/priming:stable
        command: ["/app/priming","--dataset","s3://private-deploy/priming/{{TENANT_ID}}.ndjson","--qps","0.1"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 2

Troubleshooting quick reference (top issues):
- If p95 spikes after handoff: check kv_cache_hit_rate and network egress throttles.
- If telemetry not received: verify agent certificate (openssl s_client -connect telemetry.ingest:443) and operator vault key rotation timestamp.
- If priming job OOMs: increase priming job memory by 1.5x and reduce concurrency.

Validation checklist (operator signoff):
1. All preflight indicators green.
2. Model artifact fingerprint stored in tenant evidence bundle.
3. Synthetic probe pass (3/3).
4. Metrics and trace spans visible in tenant dashboard with correct labels.
5. Handoff notification sent and ticket closed with acceptance tags.

Audit and evidence preservation:
- The operator must archive the following artifacts to the tenant evidence bucket: preflight-<TENANT_ID>.json, model.sha256, priming-job.log, healthcheck.json, and the final handoff email template. Retention default 365 days.

Related pages and references:
- See onboarding runbook and private-deploy evidence checklist for accepted artifact formats.
- Implementation notes: contact eng-private-deployments team for operator CLI flags and to request additional priming datasets.

Appendix A — Operator handoff email template (example):
Subject: Tenant <TENANT_ID> — Initialization complete
Body: Tenant <TENANT_ID> has completed initialization. Key artifacts: preflight report link, model fingerprint, priming logs. Observability: metrics streaming = yes, synthetic probes = 3/3. Next steps: schedule QBR with customer.
